messages.subject: RStan CRAN-like "home" page
parts:
Even though we're not on CRAN, would users
find a CRAN-like home page more inviting?

If the HTML gets generated automatically I can
drop it onto our web site.

I was also thinking it'd give us a natural place
to put (a) the vignette, and (b) the PDF doc
for the package. (I hate the R online help
navigation.)

No need to do this for 1.0.3 -- I want to release
1.0.3. ASAP.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan CRAN-like "home" page
parts:
On 10/26/12 7:34 AM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> In addition, if it is helpful, I can build the rstan package doc in html and put them on the web.

That would be great. Then when users did a web
search for an issue, they'd find it.

> On Thu, Oct 25, 2012 at 8:58 PM, Jiqiang Guo <guo...@gmail.com <mailto:guo...@gmail.com>> wrote:
>
> That Cran webpage for each package is not generated when building rstan package. It would not be hard for us to
> generate one since most of it is from the description. But where are we going to put it and use where we have a
> link pointing to it to make it more inviting?

It'd be easiest to put a link under the "Manual / Examples"
section of the home page. It would also make sense to link from
the Wiki.

We could also give RStan it's own home page with more links
on it. I think we're going to need that eventually as things
get added.

The links will also help search engines uprank it.

- Bob
